answer: A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. Histories are stored in beacon, checked in lantern, and willow exposes each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 2 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm of 1930 identities would post 4560 proofs and burn roughly 10 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
